The defendant, Ng Sui-ting (伍瑞庭), appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black mask. The charges allege that on 10 July and 17 August respectively, the defendant allowed a large male yellow mongrel dog to enter the area around Yuen Long YOHO Mall without being held on a leash no longer than two metres. He faces two counts of "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place."

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks for mention, and did not oppose bail. Acting Chief Magistrate Tang Siu-hung (鄧少雄) agreed to adjourn the case to 29 October for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

Under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation (《危險狗隻規例》), a conviction for "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place" carries a fine of HK$25,000 and three months' imprisonment.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), Yip Yin (葉彥), said yesterday that if the dog's owner decides to surrender the animal to the government, the department would consider options including humane euthanasia; if the owner intends to take the dog back, the dog may be classified as a "known dangerous dog," and the court may order that it must wear a muzzle whenever it goes out in future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection group Mao Shou Rescue (毛守救援), told The Collective (《集誌社》) that the dog's owner regrets signing the surrender document; he also said Mao Shou is willing to take in the dog and provide a dog trainer to rehabilitate it.
